tagbot.title: TagBot
tagbot.description: Educational robotics robot built on an ESP32, controlled via a Flutter app over BLE/WiFi, with an onboard camera and 6 operating modes. Showcased in partnership with Brazil's Federal Revenue Service, with future use in schools planned.
tagbot.n_intro: Educational robotics robot built on an ESP32, controlled via a Flutter app over BLE/WiFi, with an onboard camera and 6 operating modes. Showcased in partnership with Brazil's Federal Revenue Service, with future use in schools planned.
tagbot.n_resultado_body: Working prototype built and tested, with a published Android control app (Flutter) and 6 operating modes: digital control (D-pad + sequence), joystick, autonomous geometric shapes, gyroscope control (phone tilt), timed commands (timer), and direct motor speed control (PWM). The project was showcased in partnership with Brazil's Federal Revenue Service, a meaningful institutional milestone for NERo, plus a public demo at Semana do Fazendeiro (UFV). Use in schools is planned as the project's next phase.
tagbot.n_contexto_body: Teaching robotics in Brazilian basic education runs into cost barriers and a lack of adapted teaching material. NERo/UFV proposed TagBot as a low-cost educational robotics platform, designed to eventually be brought into schools as a hands-on tool for introducing programming and robotics. As a validation and outreach step, TagBot was showcased in partnership with Brazil's Federal Revenue Service and at Semana do Fazendeiro (UFV).
tagbot.n_construido_body: C++ firmware on the ESP32 via PlatformIO, with a modular architecture separating sensor/actuator drivers, the control layer, and the communication layer. The Flutter Android app exposes the 6 control modes (Digital, Joystick, Geometry (autonomous geometric paths), Gyroscope (control via the phone's accelerometer tilt), Timer (timed commands), and PWM (direct motor speed control)), with a live connection-status indicator (TAGBOT-01 · ONLINE) and telemetry readout. Communication is dual: native ESP32 BLE and WiFi via a repurposed TV-box module, giving redundancy and extended range.
tagbot.n_hardware_body: A USB camera module (C3Tech Full HD 1080p) mounted on the robot, a likely base for future computer-vision work. An ultrasonic sensor (HC-SR04) for obstacle detection, a line sensor for line-following, and encoders (E2-Q2) for odometry, all wired into firmware across the app's operating modes.

asimav.title: AsiMAV
asimav.description: NERo/UFV's autonomous drone system for the Flying Robot League at CBR 2026. Team captain, leading the software, development, and testing of the project.
asimav.n_intro: NERo/UFV's autonomous drone system for the Flying Robot League at CBR 2026. Team captain, leading the software, development, and testing of the project.
asimav.n_resultado_body: Still open: the competition takes place in November 2026 in João Pessoa/PB, and the team is currently in the Phase 1 preparation stage.
asimav.n_contexto_body: RoboCup Brazil's Flying Robot League challenges teams to build autonomous UAVs (no GPS, no external control) capable of recognizing landing pads by vision, carrying cargo, interacting with humans via gestures, and navigating confined spaces. AsiMAV is NERo/UFV's answer to that challenge, built by a team with mostly no prior experience in flying systems.
asimav.n_construido_body: The project is still at an early stage, working through Phase 1 of the competition. The planned architecture uses ROS2 and Gazebo for simulation, pyparrot to control the real drone (Bebop 2), and OpenCV for computer vision. As captain, I'm mainly responsible for the project's software, development, and testing.

capybot.title: Capybot
capybot.description: Stationary social-reception robot with a capybara-inspired design, using a local LLM and STT/TTS for natural interaction with visitors.
capybot.n_intro: Stationary social-reception robot with a capybara-inspired design, using a local LLM and STT/TTS for natural interaction with visitors.
capybot.n_resultado_body: MVP1 architecture fully closed and validated: the voice pipeline (VAD → STT → LLM → TTS), facial recognition, and local RAG are all defined end to end. Final LLM model selection is still pending a latency/RAM benchmark on the Raspberry Pi 5.
capybot.n_contexto_body: Capybot is the first of three progressive robots under Projeto R2D2, my own research project that I proposed and got approved at NERo/UFV. It serves as a proof of concept for 100% local human-robot interaction, with no cloud dependency, before scaling up to mobile robotics (Sentinel-X) and active-response systems (Aegis). The core challenge is running multimodal perception (voice, vision, LLM) under embedded hardware constraints while keeping response latency low.
capybot.n_construido_body: A voice pipeline with activity detection (silero-vad) and transcription (faster-whisper) feeding an intent classifier (sentence-transformers) that runs in parallel with the LLM via asyncio.gather, cutting perceived latency. Facial recognition via InsightFace (buffalo_sc). Context and memory via RAG with sqlite-vec, chosen over ChromaDB for its lower overhead on embedded hardware. Multimodal vision models are loaded and unloaded sequentially to keep RAM usage in check on the RPi 5. Voice output via Piper TTS; LCD visual states are statically pre-rendered via pygame to avoid real-time rendering cost. Servo control via ESP32, communicating with the RPi 5 over WebSocket. Technical leadership on architecture decisions alongside Cauan, as NERo organizers.
capybot.n_hardware_body: Raspberry Pi 5 (8GB), ESP32, servos, and a 3.5-inch LCD display.

fluxo.title: Fluxo
fluxo.description: Operational-intelligence web platform for restaurants in event-driven cities: measures queue and service in real time and converts overload into lost revenue before it happens.
fluxo.n_intro: Operational-intelligence web platform for restaurants in event-driven cities: measures queue and service in real time and converts overload into lost revenue before it happens.
fluxo.n_resultado_body: 3rd place at Hackathon Abrasel, organized by TecnoPARQ, held August 21–23, 2026 in Viçosa, MG.
fluxo.n_contexto_body: Viçosa is a university town whose commerce lives off demand spikes tied to events. The Semana do Fazendeiro fair alone draws around 134,000 visitors over 9 days (more than 42,000 in the first weekend alone), yet local restaurants still size staff and stock by eye. The problem isn't a lack of forecasting for the city, it's that no restaurant measures its own operation in real time: 89% of industry business owners report difficulty hiring qualified labor (ABRASEL/Panrotas, 2024), 40% of customers abandon the line after 15 minutes with no wait estimate (Sebrae/WiFire, 2025), and 62.7% of establishments in the sector close within 5 years (IBGE, 2024). Enterprise tools like Toast or Restaurant365 start at R$2,500/month per unit, out of reach for a small or mid-size restaurant.
fluxo.n_construido_body: Fluxo is a real-time web platform where staff log the customer's full cycle (queue, table, order, delivery) on simple 1-2 tap screens, with no new hardware in anyone's pocket. A pure decision engine on the backend turns these events into real queueing-theory metrics: λ/μ (arrival and service rates via EWMA over live events, not modeled or estimated), Wq (actually measured wait), overload projection via Erlang C, and direct conversion into R$ at risk. Every decision (color, estimated time, normal/attention/urgent recommendation) is computed once on the backend and distributed over WebSocket as a full snapshot to every screen: the dashboard, the customer's table tablet, and the two phones running the operations panel are all just thin renderers of that same truth.
fluxo.n_hardware_body: A laser-cut tablet stand was built for the customer-facing table view (triangular prism, coffee-brown + terracotta palette, with a fixed "Call waiter" button). The operations panel that covers the 4 urgency categories for staff runs on two regular phones over the web, with no fabrication needed.

robosPlatform.title: Robótica // Hub
robosPlatform.description: Unofficial hub for UFV's Robotics Engineering (ERO) program, bringing together an interactive curriculum graph, a study-material archive, and a calendar of exams and semester events in one place.
robosPlatform.n_intro: Unofficial hub for UFV's Robotics Engineering (ERO) program, bringing together an interactive curriculum graph, a study-material archive, and a calendar of exams and semester events in one place.
robosPlatform.n_resultado_body: The platform is complete and live. The curriculum graph renders all 55 courses in the program with their full prerequisite and corequisite relationships, navigable by zoom, pan, search, and a minimap. The Archive already holds dozens of study materials (exams, problem sets, summaries, slides, and books), organized by semester and course, synced automatically from a shared Google Drive folder. The upload flow lets any student in the program send multiple files, of different types, in a single batch, straight to Drive, with no manual form involved. The calendar pulls exams, deadlines, and due dates from a Google Sheet maintained by the class, so it stays current without touching any code. The plan is to keep evolving it gradually, adding features as students' needs come up over the semesters.
robosPlatform.n_contexto_body: UFV's Robotics Engineering program didn't have a central place where students could clearly see the curriculum's structure (which courses depend on which, what semester to take each one), nor a single place to gather and share study material produced by the class itself over the semesters. Information was scattered across WhatsApp groups, loose Drive folders, and the university's PDF curriculum. This project started as a personal initiative, with no institutional tie to NERo, to solve that problem in a simple, visual way.
robosPlatform.n_construido_body: Robótica // Hub is a Vue 3 SPA with its own minimal routing system (no vue-router, due to a dependency conflict with the beta version of Vue used in the project), covering five main pages. The Graph is an interactive canvas that draws the program's 55 courses as nodes connected by their prerequisite and corequisite dependencies, with zoom, pan, course search, and a minimap for orientation across a large curriculum. The Archive is a study-material repository organized by semester and type (exams, problem sets, summaries, slides, books), with data synced automatically from a Google Drive folder by a script that runs in CI, keeping the site current with no manual work. Upload is a form gated by a shared access password, validated entirely server-side by a Vercel serverless function and never exposed in the browser bundle, which authenticates via OAuth with the Google account that owns the folder and generates a resumable-upload URL for the browser itself to send the file straight to Google Drive, working around the payload limit of serverless functions, with support for multiple files and material types in a single submission. The Calendar loads semester events (exams, deadlines, due dates) dynamically from a Google Sheet published as CSV, letting the class keep the calendar current without a deploy. And Links gathers useful UFV resources and services for students in the program. I was responsible for the project, from design and architecture through development and publishing.

terrasafe.title: TerraSafe
terrasafe.description: Low-cost IoT sensor network for soil moisture monitoring on slopes, developed during the SmartCamp Cidades Inteligentes bootcamp, June 13–14, 2026, TecnoParque UFV.
terrasafe.n_intro: Low-cost IoT sensor network for soil moisture monitoring on slopes, developed during the SmartCamp Cidades Inteligentes bootcamp, June 13–14, 2026, TecnoParque UFV.
terrasafe.n_resultado_body: 1st place at SmartCamp Cidades Inteligentes, a bootcamp organized by the Viçosa SMART project in partnership with LabMAKER and VUEI/UFV. Prize: R$ 2,000.
terrasafe.n_contexto_body: Brazil's Zona da Mata recorded 72 confirmed deaths in landslides in February 2026, with 5,500 people displaced and 752 mm of accumulated rainfall in a single month in Juiz de Fora, an INMET record. Forecasting systems like INMET's predict when it will rain, but they don't indicate when soil is saturated enough to give way. 50 mm of rain on dry soil doesn't have the same effect as 50 mm on already-saturated soil, and that difference is not captured by a rain alert.
terrasafe.n_construido_body: TerraSafe monitors soil conditions directly, rather than just predicting rain. Each probe sits partially buried in the slope (~80 cm) and measures soil moisture, slope angle (via accelerometer), air temperature, and humidity. Readings leave the probe over an ESP-NOW mesh network, no Wi-Fi router needed, reach a local hub, and travel over serial to a FastAPI backend that updates a live map in real time and generates alerts when saturation crosses the configured threshold.
terrasafe.n_hardware_body: ESP32 as the microcontroller, capacitive soil moisture sensor, DHT11 for temperature and air humidity, MPU6050 for slope angle, and an 18650 Li-Ion battery for field autonomy. Cost per unit: R$ 60–80.
terrasafe.n_escala_body: The prototype presented at the hackathon ran with 1 to 3 sensors, covering the full flow from sensor to alert. The planned roadmap includes a municipal pilot with 50 to 200 sensors at risk points mapped by Viçosa's Defesa Civil, regional scale with 1,000 to 5,000 sensors integrated with SGB and CEMADEN, and eventually a SaaS model for municipalities.
